jobs.excerpt: Why Charlie Health? Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care.
jobs.description:
Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is hiring exceptional candidates with a Masters degree in mental health and previous work experience facilitating groups to provide remote, telehealth services to our adolescent and young adult clients. We’re eager to work with forward-thinking mental health professionals to enhance our programming and provide the best possible care to our clients.

People know Charlie Health for our warm and empathetic clinical team. While each individual clinician has their own interests, expertise, and style, we require all team members to be well versed in a variety of modalities. Our clients are struggling to cope with underlying mental health issues and benefit from therapists that are sophisticated and relational. Successful candidates are committed to bettering the mental health of their clients, along with being adept at self-care, ensuring they are prepared to give their best every day to address the youth mental health crisis.

Responsibilities

  • Complete all Onboarding requirements within 2 weeks of start date
  • Meet with your assigned Charlie Health Group Quality Supervisor or Group Quality Director at a minimum of 1x/month for required check-in
  • Respond to all email and Slack communication promptly (within 48 hours of receiving a communication)
  • Review the curriculum aligned to group assignment prior to group start time
  • Arrive ~10 minutes early to scheduled group time and facilitate all groups for the entirety of the hour
  • Facilitate groups following Charlie Health best practices and using assigned and most up to date Charlie Health curriculum
  • Facilitate groups across age groups and cohorts, including Integrative curriculum, Support Staffing and Wellness Hour as needed
  • Foster client engagement and group cohesion throughout the session, encouraging client participation and fostering camera-on culture
  • Following all operational policies and procedures as indicated by Charlie Health best practices
  • Participate in collaborative Treatment Team (Tuesdays) and Group Supervision (every other Friday) with your assigned Charlie Health Group Quality Supervisor or Group Quality Director, peers and other Clinical Leadership team members
  • Work collaboratively and respectfully across the care team including with Primary Therapists, Care Experience Specialists and Care Coaches
  • Communicate clearly, professionally, and promptly with all clients, staff, families, agencies, and referents
  • Monitor your treatment documentation to ensure all of your notes are completed within required 24 hour timeframe and meet agency and professional standards per DHCS and The Joint Commission standards
  • Maintain and model professional ethics, including appropriate boundaries and confidentiality
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements

  • Must be available during late afternoons and evenings on weekdays (3-8pm MT on Monday to Thursday) and on Saturdays to meet the schedules of our adolescent and young adult clients
  • Master’s degree in mental health or related field required (see below for full list)
  • Experience working with youth and young adults
  • Well versed in a variety of modalities and feel confident integrating them into your treatment approach (DBT, CBT, EMDR, MI certification is a plus)
  • Passionate about the benefits of group treatment and skilled in conducting group treatment
  • Ability to work effectively in a team
  • Creative and engaging, especially over video!
  • The technical ability to run effective telehealth sessions
  • Reliable WIFI connection when meeting with clients
  • Familiarity with and willingness to use cloud-based communication software—Gmail, Slack, Zoom, Dropbox–in addition to EMR and outcomes survey software on a daily basis
  • Part time 1099 role

Benefits

  • Charlie Health is pleased to offer comprehensive benefits to all full-time, exempt employees. Read more about our benefits here.

Eligible Master's Degrees:

  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Mental Health Counseling
  • Master of Arts (M.A.) in Counseling Psychology
  • Master of Social Work (M.S.W.) with a concentration in Mental Health
  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Clinical Mental Health Counseling
  • Master of Arts (M.A.) in Marriage and Family Therapy
  • Master of Arts (M.A.) in Clinical Psychology
  • Master of Science (M.S.) in School Counseling
  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Rehabilitation Counseling
  • Master of Science (M.S.) in Applied Developmental Psychology
  • Master of Arts (M.A) in Education (with experience in behavioral health)
  • Master of Education (Ed.M) (with experience in behavioral health)

Based on the nature of this role, you will need to complete several state background checks for clearance to see clients. Florida requires a fingerprint based background check, with more information found here. Please note that the cost for this background check will be paid for in full by Charlie Health.

Bright Vision Technologies is a technology consulting and software development company delivering cloud, AI, data, and enterprise solutions across the United States.
This is a fantastic opportunity to join an established and well-respected organization offering tremendous career growth potential.

Job Title: Cloud Networking Engineer
Location: 100% Remote (U.S.)
Position Type: Full-time, Direct W2
Salary Range: $100,000–$150,000 Annually
Experience Required: 6+ years

Sponsorship: U.S. Citizens, Green Card Holders, EAD Holders, and H-1B transfer candidates are encouraged to apply. We are unable to sponsor new H-1B visa petitions for this position.

Job Summary
We are looking for a Cloud Networking Engineer to design, deploy, and operate service mesh platforms — primarily Istio and Linkerd — that provide secure, observable, and reliable service-to-service communication across our Kubernetes estate. The role focuses on platform engineering, mesh adoption, mTLS, traffic policy, and helping application teams reap the benefits of a mesh without paying for unnecessary complexity. The ideal candidate has operated service mesh in production, deeply understands Envoy and the data plane, and brings both platform engineering discipline and pragmatic adoption strategies.

Required Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Five or more years of experience in platform engineering, SRE, or networking roles.
  • Hands-on experience operating Istio or Linkerd in production.
  • Strong understanding of Envoy proxy internals and configuration.
  • Deep Kubernetes expertise including networking, CNI, and ingress.
  • Strong understanding of mTLS, PKI, and certificate lifecycle management.
  • Experience with distributed tracing and observability for mesh traffic.
  • Proficiency in Go or Python for tooling and automation.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across networking, application, and control plane layers.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills.
Preferred Qualifications
  • Experience with multi-cluster Istio or Linkerd deployments.
  • Familiarity with Cilium service mesh and eBPF networking.
  • Open-source contributions to service mesh projects.
  • Experience with SPIFFE/SPIRE for workload identity.
  • Exposure to zero-trust networking initiatives at enterprise scale.

About the Role

We're hiring a Staff Software Engineer to own architecture and design decisions for our platform, including the modernization of legacy enterprise systems into modern, cloud-capable solutions. You'll operate with significant autonomy, act as a force multiplier for the rest of the engineering team, work closely with our Head of R&D as a technical backup, and be a candidate for broader technical responsibility across projects as you prove yourself. This is a hands-on, high-ownership role on a lean, three-person engineering team — small enough that your architectural calls ship and show results in weeks, not after months of committee review. You'll be a player-coach: as comfortable writing code as setting direction, designing and deciding as well as implementing, delegating, and growing the engineers around you. In an AI-assisted development era, we value sound judgment and design thinking as much as implementation speed — you'll have real latitude to use tools like Claude and Cursor to move faster, not just permission to.

Responsibilities

Architecture & Technical Ownership

  • Own architecture and design decisions for the systems you're responsible for, favoring pragmatic, right-sized solutions over unnecessary complexity, and weighing trade-offs (build vs. buy, hosted vs. on-premises, integration approach) with senior-level judgment.
  • Lead the modernization of legacy systems into maintainable, cloud-capable architectures without disrupting the business relying on them.
  • Review requirements and designs early to flag architectural risk, technical debt, and feasibility gaps before they become expensive.
  • Own solution-level architecture documentation — decisions, trade-offs, and the reasoning behind them — so the system stays understandable at a glance, not just in your head.

Hands-On Delivery

  • Design and implement significant parts of the system yourself — this role ships production code, not just plans.
  • Own what you build end-to-end, including its health after it ships — if it breaks in production, you're part of fixing it.
  • Apply AI-assisted development tools (e.g., Claude, Cursor) to work faster across design, implementation, and documentation, with informed judgment about where they genuinely help.

Team Leadership & Mentorship

  • Delegate work effectively and help pull the wider team forward, rather than carrying everything yourself.
  • Mentor other engineers through code review, design discussion, and day-to-day guidance, as an individual contributor rather than a people manager.
  • Act as a technical backup to the Head of R&D, and take on broader technical responsibility across projects over time.

Product & Customer Judgment

  • Translate ambiguous customer needs — including regulated-industry and enterprise requirements — into sound technical designs.
  • Work closely with product owners, QA, and subject-matter experts to understand how the product is used and where the real risk lies.
  • Communicate trade-offs, risks, and plans clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Ways of Working

  • Operate independently in ambiguous, shifting-priority conditions, setting your own priorities rather than waiting to be told what's next.
  • This role has no fixed lane — architecture, hands-on coding, mentoring, production support, whatever's needed. You pick it up rather than waiting for it to be assigned.
  • Participate in and help shape Agile ceremonies (stand-ups, sprint planning, retrospectives).

Our Stack

Description

Join a Company That Invests in You

Seeking Alpha is the world's leading community of engaged investors. We’re the go-to destination for investors looking for actionable stock market opinions, real-time market analysis, and unique financial insights. At the same time, we’re also dedicated to creating a workplace where our team thrives. We’re passionate about fostering a flexible, balanced environment with remote work options and an array of perks that make a real difference.

What We're Looking For

Do you look at websites and think about how they might be personalized? Do you use websites and apps and think about how their features have been designed to be best for a lot of different users? Do you read articles with statistics and think about how they may be misinterpreting the data to get their results? If these things describe you, and if you’re great at SQL and have experience analyzing website data, you’re someone we want to talk to.

We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst with experience analyzing website data. Our data analyst team analyzes everything on our website, not only for their immediate use but also for how they connect to high-level company KPIs. Our Analysts analyze raw data, not only pre-aggregated data, to extract just the right information and diagnose what is happening on our site.

The role requires understanding web development and how data is gathered, analysis of site usage and a/b tests, data visualization, and how different kinds of data can be presented most clearly, and business KPIs and how they are measured.

But more than that, we’re looking for experienced analysts who can bring us new ideas about how to analyze and extract insights from website data. Our ideal candidates have measured KPIs that we haven’t measured or used new ways to explain user retention, or analyzed features of users' data that we haven’t analyzed.

The best thing about our work is that we’re part of an incredibly data-driven company. Everyone from the CEO down uses data every day. The data teams are involved in every single thing the company does.

The Senior Data Analyst will be engaged with the company as a contractor (Private Entrepreneur).

What You'll Do

  • Analyzing the behavior of users on our site and apps:

-Build and maintain dashboards that visualize the usage of single or multiple features and how that usage drives company KPIs.

-Answer questions about site usage or user behavior based on deeper analyses.

  • Analyze and track high-level KPIs such as conversion, retention, churn, recurring revenue, engagement, cross-device usage, e-mail and notification usage, and more.
  • Communicate with business stakeholders on analysis results, how they relate to business, and what business suggestions result from the analysis.
  • Run the whole data flow for site and app features, from defining KPIs, specifying data collection for development team implementation, and building and maintaining iterative versions of dashboards with both low-level and high-level views of collected data.
  • Split tests of product features:

-Design a test with clear success criteria

-Monitor test integrity

-Analyze results and give recommendations

-Use segmentation and clear cohort analysis to validate significant conclusions

-Conduct exploratory analysis to identify trends and opportunities

Requirements

  • A minimum of 5 years in a B2C website-related Data Analyst position
  • Strong SQL skills with experience writing complex and efficient analytical queries
  • Demonstrated experience with working in English directly with business stakeholders, understanding their needs, and explaining results
  • Understanding of website development and operations and how they connect to data gathered.
  • Experience with data visualization tools (Looker/Tableau/PowerBI, etc.)
  • Experience with report writing and technical requirements analysis, business process modeling/mapping, methodology development, and data modeling

Take Charge of Your Career at Interstates

At Interstates, we don’t just show up to work, we show up for each other. Summary: The VDC Planner partners with internal teams, subcontractors, and clients to plan and coordinate virtual design and construction (VDC) activities that improve productivity, safety, and project efficiency. This role applies technical knowledge of electrical installation practices to define VDC scope, support prefabrication planning, and align deliverables with project schedules. The VDC Planner provides guidance to project teams, mentors designers and technicians, resolves field coordination issues, and drives continuous improvement in VDC processes and standards through collaboration, technology adoption, and lessons learned.

Responsibilities:

  • Assist with VDC coordination for subcontractors, offering basic guidance and support as needed.

  • Mentor team members in design best practices by reviewing work, collaborating on projects, and delegating designs for BIM modelling.
  • Resolves field issues by collaborating with field leaders to identify challenges and propose solutions.
  • Assesses project risks and mitigation strategies through review of project documentation.
  • Provide feedback to technicians and designers by reviewing deliverables and communicating necessary adjustments.
  • Identify and implement process improvements in VDC workflows by applying lessons learned to enhance efficiency and drive continuous improvement.

Qualifications: To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education and/or Experience: A bachelor’s degree in electrical construction management or a related technical field is preferred; however, candidates with an associate degree and substantial experience in electrical planning or construction will also be considered. The ideal candidate will have a Journeyman's license with 3-5 years of experience in electrical planning, design, or construction coordination, with hands-on involvement in electrical systems such as power distribution, lighting, and low-voltage installations. A strong understanding of the National Electrical Code (NEC) and other relevant industry standards is essential. Candidates should have experience in project planning, including material takeoffs and resource scheduling, and demonstrate the ability to collaborate effectively with project managers, field teams, and other stakeholders to ensure the accurate planning and execution of electrical work. This position requires strong computer skills, good organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to prioritize work, and deal with stress. Must possess the ability to work cooperatively with others. Must have a basic understanding of internal controls. Must be able to maintain a high standard of professionalism and confidentiality of critical issues. Must be able to handle the work schedule and attendance policies required at Interstates. Strong understanding of construction processes, project management principles, and building codes. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work effectively in a multidisciplinary team environment.

Travel Requirements: Travel will be required and will vary according to business requirements. Travel should not exceed 35% of your time.

Compensation: The pay range for this position is $70,040 to $88,000+ benefits. Our salary ranges are determined by the experience and education required, and level of responsibility. The range posted for this role represents a range that Interstates, in good faith, believes it is willing to pay at the time of this posting. The pay is determined by job related skills, training, education, and experience.

This will ensure your application is considered in the initial review process. Applications received after this date may be considered depending on the status of the search.

What You Should Know Before You Apply

Interstates may collect personal information as part of your job application, such as your contact details, work history, education, and any information you provide. This information is used only for recruitment, to evaluate your candidacy, and to meet legal requirements. For details about our privacy practices and your rights under the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), please see our Privacy Policy. By applying, you acknowledge that you have reviewed this notice.

Interstates is an EEO provider and offers a drug-free workplace. Employment at Interstates is at-will and may be terminated at any time with or without notice or cause, except as otherwise provided by law.

Talkspace is a leading virtual behavioral healthcare provider committed to helping people lead healthier, happier lives through access to high-quality mental healthcare. At Talkspace, we believe that mental healthcare is core to overall health and should be available to everyone.

Talkspace pioneered the ability to text with a licensed therapist from anywhere and now offers a comprehensive suite of mental health services, including therapy for individuals, teens, and couples, as well as psychiatric treatment and medication management (18+). EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

The ideal candidate will have a strong understanding of translation best practices, experience with CAT tools such as Smartling and bug-tracking tools such as Jira, and practical experience using LLMs and AI-assisted translation. Strategy & Program Management

Requirements

jobs.description:
Job Title: Manager, Business Development
Reports to: Deputy Director, Foundations and Corporates
Location: Fully Remote: USA based - US Eastern or Central time zone preferred. Availability 8:00 am - 4:00 pm ET for overlap with East Africa, West Africa and Europe.

About Living Goods:
Community health is one of the most proven ways to save lives. But as community health systems scale, many struggle to maintain quality, control costs, and deliver consistent results. Scale without performance puts lives at risk.

Living Goods is a government performance partner that supports countries in Africa to build affordable, intelligent, high-impact community health systems. For almost 20 years, we have worked alongside the governments of Kenya, Uganda, and Burkina Faso to make community health work at scale. Our work focuses on aligning policies, financing, technology, and workforce to turn government investment into consistent, reliable, quality care for families. Our approach is research-proven, built for real-world constraints, and delivers life-saving care for about $2 per person served.

As global health funding tightens and expectations for measurable results grow, governments need systems they can afford, sustain, and manage for results. Our 2027–2030 strategy is built for this moment. It focuses on strengthening the operating foundations of government-led systems, scaling proven solutions, and developing new approaches to emerging challenges, including intelligent systems that use data and AI to better support government community health workers (CHWs) and the systems around them.

Our vision is simple: when families need healthcare, it’s there. Not eventually. Not only when a program reaches them. But reliably—through systems designed to work, improve, and endure.

The Opportunity:
Living Goods is seeking a Manager, Business Development to build the philanthropic partnerships in the U.S. market that make our 2027–2030 strategy possible. You will identify, cultivate, secure, and steward multi-year investments from US-based foundations and corporate funders, with a focus on larger and technically complex opportunities. You will keep funders engaged and invested over time, building the relationships and results reporting that drive renewals and increased giving.

This is a role for an experienced fundraiser who is ready to carry a meaningful share of our revenue target and to step into senior funder conversations. You will own your portfolio of relationships, lead the proposals behind them, and sharpen how we tell the Living Goods performance story to U.S. funders.

You will report to the Deputy Director, Foundations and Corporates, and work closely with colleagues across Business Development, Programs, Innovations, Digital Health, Finance, Advocacy, and Communications in East and West Africa, the U.S., and Europe.

You will thrive in this role if...

  • You build enduring relationships.
You are comfortable leading a funder meeting, not just supporting one. You can find the overlap between a funder's priorities and ours, adjust your message for each audience, and keep a relationship warm through the long stretches of a 12-to-24-month cultivation cycle.
  • You can go deep when the conversation gets technical.
A program officer at a large funder will ask about unit economics, scale pathways, government integration, and evidence. You can give a substantive answer, and you know when and how to bring in technical colleagues from other departments when needed to go deeper.
  • You run complex proposals with accuracy and confidence.
You manage up, down, and across the organization to coordinate winning proposals. You anticipate the next step, get the inputs you need from Finance, Programs, and Compliance, make judgement calls on what goes in, and push back-on colleagues when the proposal needs it.
  • You are agile.
You can pitch a plan that is still taking shape, and you don't need perfectly settled materials to move a relationship forward. You are resourceful, rigorous about priorities, and calm under tight external deadlines. You seek feedback and use it and are excited to build a career in an organization that is changing quickly.

Responsibilities:
Relationship ownership and revenue
  • Own a portfolio of existing and prospective U.S. foundation and corporate donors. This is an externally facing role with direct revenue responsibility toward the team's annual funding target.
  • Build and carry out engagement strategies to retain donors and secure new and increased funding, including larger, multi-year, restricted awards.
  • Represent Living Goods in conversations with funders, including technical discussions on our approach, evidence base, unit economics, and path to scale.
  • Position Living Goods to win funding from large, technically complex foundations, corporate funders, funder collaboratives and pooled mechanisms by building relationships with funders, shaping our case for support, and pursuing opportunities as they open.
  • Support the CEO and other leaders in funder engagements, making sure leadership is well-prepared for every funder interaction.

Proposal Leadership
  • Lead and project manage concept notes and full proposals, coordinating technical input from Programs and Digital Health, budgets with Finance, compliance review, and leadership engagement.
  • Guide donor due diligence and the negotiation of restricted terms and reporting requirements, working with Finance and Compliance.
  • Facilitate strategic decisions on which funding and partnership opportunities to pursue and what the most compelling pitch for Living Goods would be, aligned with funder interests.
  • Support opportunities to bid with partners, such as implementers and technology providers, where a joint approach strengthens our competitiveness.
Pipeline, reporting, and strategy
  • Monitor opportunities and contribute to pipeline forecasting and donor surveillance across the U.S. market.
  • Advise on grant reporting for your portfolio, sharing what each funder cares about and how they like to receive results, so reports are tailored to the donor.
  • Work with the grant writer and Communications team to create and update funder communications and collateral that reflect Living Goods' messaging.
  • Contribute to U.S.-market strategy, including how the team positions our 2027–2030 strategy to funders and test new fundraising approaches and partnership models.

Qualifications and Experience:
Required
  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field.
  • 5 - 7 years of experience in fundraising or business development, including at least 2–3 years at manager level or in a role with comparable portfolio ownership.
  • Personal ownership of significant ($1M+) awards, from cultivation through signed agreement and into future renewals. We are looking for relationship ownership, not only contribution to a team effort.
  • Direct experience with institutional funder processes, including introductory meetings, pitch/co-creation discussions, concept notes, full proposals, due diligence, and negotiation of grant terms and requirements.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multi-stakeholder proposal development across program, finance, and compliance functions, producing high-quality work under tight deadlines.
  • Experience in global health, international development, or an adjacent technical field sufficient to hold substantive conversations with donors.
  • Exceptional writing and communication skills, with the ability to develop clear and convincing materials that are attentive to nuance and audience.
  • Experience with budgeting and financial reporting.
  • Collaborative spirit, demonstrated by active listening, clear communication, being a team player, and earning trust across departments, with executive team members, country teams, and peers.
  • Willingness to travel domestically and internationally, likely 2-3 times per year.

Preferred
  • Existing relationships or credible networks among large U.S. global health foundations and corporate philanthropy, including technology and pharmaceutical companies.
  • Technical fluency in global health, digital health, or health systems, enough to engage credibly on program design.
  • Experience with funder collaboratives or pooled funds.

Compensation
A competitive salary and benefits package commensurate with experience including health insurance and annual performance bonus pay opportunity. This is an opportunity to be your best while making lives better for those in need!

Living Goods is an equal opportunity employer and will consider every qualified applicant for employment. Living Goods does not discriminate based on race, ethnicity, national origin, ancestry, religion, gender, sexual orientation or disability.

Our current job openings are displayed on our website, where you can search for open positions and apply directly. Living Goods does not offer any positions without an interview and never asks candidates for money. If you are asked for money, we strongly recommend that you do not respond and do not send money or personal information.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Mental Health Therapist (Bilingual)(Contractor)

Reports To: Clinical Supervisor

Position Type: Full-Time

Department: OMHC Department

Location: Hybrid OR Remote

Pay Rate: $55-65/Hour

Position Summary

Synergy Family Services is seeking a skilled, responsive, and growth-oriented Outpatient Mental Health Therapist to provide high-quality therapy within our community-based OMHC program. This role is designed for a clinician who understands that excellent care includes both what happens in session and the consistent work surrounding it: engagement, treatment planning, documentation, care coordination, timely communication, and follow-through.

The Employee Therapist manages an assigned caseload, provides individual and family therapy, monitors whether clients are receiving services at the frequency identified through intake and treatment planning, and works collaboratively across Synergy programs. The successful candidate is clinically grounded, comfortable learning technology, accountable to deadlines, open to supervision and feedback, and motivated to continually strengthen their practice.

Core Essential Responsibilities

  • Provide individual and family therapy using evidence-based, trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and person-centered approaches.
  • Assess client needs, strengths, risks, diagnoses, functioning, and progress, translate findings into measurable treatment goals and clinically appropriate interventions.
  • Maintain continuity of care by providing sessions at the frequency established through intake, clinical need, and the treatment plan—such as twice weekly, weekly, every other week, or monthly.
  • Monitor attendance and engagement. When a client is not being seen at the expected frequency, promptly conduct and document outreach, identify barriers, collaborate with the treatment team, and follow agency re-engagement, transfer, or discharge procedures.
  • Coordinate care with supervisors and relevant internal or external partners, including Psychiatry, PRP, case management, interpreters/Family Support Workers, schools, probation officers, medical providers, and community resources.
  • Include parents, guardians, or family members when clinically appropriate and consistent with client consent, treatment goals, and agency family-session policy.
  • Recognize and respond to safety concerns, complete required risk assessments, safety plans, incident documentation, consultation, and escalation within established timeframes.
  • Support access to appropriate psychiatric, rehabilitative, case-management, and community resources when additional services are indicated.

Documentation, Technology & Workplace Accountability

  • Learn and use Credible and other required agency systems for scheduling, service documentation, communication, reporting, and workflow completion.
  • Schedule services accurately, maintain an up-to-date calendar, and finalize completed services by signing and following documentation workflows.
  • Complete clear, accurate, individualized, and clinically defensible documentation. Progress notes and GAP notes are due within three days of the service, cancellation, reschedule, or no-show.
  • Complete treatment plans, transition summaries, reassessments, Greenspace assessments, referral reviews, PRP referrals/reauthorizations, collaboration notes, transfers, discharge documentation, consents, and other assigned records within agency deadlines.
  • Correct returned documentation within three business days or the timeframe communicated by the supervisor or management.
  • Document clinically relevant calls, texts, emails, collateral contacts, outreach, barriers, and care-coordination activity in the client record.
  • Respond to agency email, telephone calls, and messages within one business day and communicate early when support or clarification is needed to meet a deadline.
  • Protect client privacy and comply with HIPAA, professional ethics, payer requirements, licensure standards, and Synergy policies and procedures.

Learning & Professional Development

  • Participate meaningfully in clinical supervision and bring cases, questions, documentation needs, ethical concerns, and skill-development goals forward for consultation.
  • Complete required onboarding, systems training, policy training, and knowledge checks by assigned deadlines.
  • Receive and apply feedback from supervision, quality review, and performance monitoring, demonstrate measurable improvement when coaching or corrective guidance is provided.
  • Maintain all required licensure, continuing education, background-check, and human-resources or contracting documentation.

Full-Time Employee Expectations

  • Meet the weekly and quarterly service expectations identified in the offer letter and current productivity policy following the established eight-week ramp-up period.
  • Maintain sufficient availability and an active caseload to support consistent productivity while accommodating reasonable client scheduling needs.
  • Submit required weekly service reporting accurately and on time, review discrepancies with the Clinical Supervisor, and resolve outstanding documentation promptly.
  • Attend mandatory meetings and trainings, participate in scheduled performance evaluations, and contribute to an assigned agency committee or initiative.
  • Work collaboratively across OMHC, Intake, Psychiatry, PRP, FSW, Quality Assurance, Human Resources, Training, and administrative teams.

Employee Benefits

  • Accrued paid time off annually - employees begin the calendar year with three (3) PTO days available.
  • Health-insurance coverage with Synergy paying 80% of individual coverage and 25% of dependent coverage.
  • Employer-provided life insurance.
  • 401(k)/pension plan eligibility after one year of employment, with an employer match of up to 3%.
  • Bonus opportunities!

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in social work, counseling, psychology, marriage and family therapy, or another related behavioral-health field from an accredited program.
  • Active Maryland license appropriate to the services provided, such as LMSW, LCSW, LCSW-C, LGPC, LCPC, LAMFT, or LMFT.
  • Knowledge of ethical, trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and person-centered behavioral-health practice.
  • Ability to assess and respond to clinical risk, maintain professional boundaries, protect confidentiality, and seek consultation appropriately.
  • Reliable access to the technology and communication methods necessary to perform the role and the ability to become proficient in an electronic health record system.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Two or more years of direct mental-health counseling or psychotherapy experience.
  • Experience in an outpatient, private practice, community-based, school-based, or Medicaid-funded behavioral-health setting.
  • Experience providing therapy to children, adolescents, adults, and/or families with diverse clinical presentations and cultural backgrounds.
  • Training or demonstrated skill in one or more evidence-based therapeutic approaches.
  • Bilingual or multilingual capability is welcomed and valued.
Salary: $55-65

Web Designer

Job Industry: Charity / Social Services / Non- Profit Organization

Role Mission

Our Rescue does not have a kennel facility or building. Our website is the only place where adopters, donors and volunteers can connect directly with us. This role designs, updates, and maintains the Path of Hope Rescue website so that it clearly communicates our mission, makes it easy for people to adopt, foster, volunteer, donate, and stay informed, and reflects a professional, welcoming, and accessible online presence.

What Winning Looks Like

Key Results Area #1 – Website Design & Visual Identity

  • Creates and maintains clean, on-brand page layouts and visual elements consistent with Path of Hope Rescue identity

  • Designs or refreshes key pages (home, adopt, volunteer, donate, events, about, etc.)

  • Ensures mobile responsiveness and a consistent look across devices

  • Selects, optimizes, and places images and graphics that support storytelling and calls to action

Key Results Area #2 – Content Integration & User Experience

  • Implements content updates (text, photos, forms, buttons) requested by other packs and leadership

  • Improves navigation, clarity of calls-to-action, and overall ease of use for visitors

  • Supports accessibility best practices (readable text, alt text, contrast, keyboard navigation where possible)

  • Collaborates with content owners to keep information accurate and current

Key Results Area #3 – Maintenance, Performance & Support

  • Performs routine checks for broken links, outdated content, and visual/layout issues

  • Optimizes page load speed and image sizes where practical

  • Documents design decisions, page structure, and simple how-tos for other volunteers

  • Responds to design and website-related requests in a timely manner

  • Recommends improvements that increase engagement, adoptions, volunteer sign-ups, or donations

Needed Skills

  • Self motivated

  • Ability to communicate remotely with excellent written communication skills

  • Ability to explain technical concepts to a non technical audience

  • Graphic Design utilizing our current brand tone and voice

  • Willing to examine current site with a critical eye and recommend changes based on UX/UI and user data

Unique Company Culture and Mission

Our Mission

At Path of Hope Rescue we save pregnant dogs and puppies from high kill shelters in the Southern United States.

Our Spokane, Washington based Rescue strives to decrease the euthanasia rate of high risk dogs in the southern United States by transporting pregnant dogs and puppies to the Pacific Northwest to find adoptive homes. We do not have a kennel or building location and are 100% foster based. We currently have two paid employees and rely heavily on volunteers and fosters as we work to build out our paid staff roles.

Our Vision.
Eliminating euthanasia of dogs in the South by decreasing the amount of dogs breeding unchecked and becoming the number one 'dog destination' in Spokane by capitalizing on Spokane's love of Rescue Dogs.

Core Values:

Transparency - sharing the good with the bad

Community - dog loving people who treat each other well

Golden Rule - treating others how you would want to be treated

Our Company Culture

We are freedom loving American Patriots who love dogs, love freedom and love Jesus.

No NGO status here, we don't take a single penny from the government. We are 100% funded by small donors and our adoption program, with a few small private grants here and there. We built this organization from the ground up in 2018 with $87.

We are built tough and believe that hard work pays off. We're about rolling up our sleeves and taking responsibility for our own actions. We don't do drama. There are no victims here and the system isn't out to get you, the only thing standing in your way is you and your attitude. We reward merit, not DEI or pronouns. We don't bend to the cultural rot out there.

At the core of who we are, we love dogs. At PHR you will find people who recognize your dog before they recognize you. Where it's normal for your dog to have his own Instagram and people who expect to be invited to your dog's birthday party. We are focused on building a strong, positive community, one dog and one person at a time.

We know dogs are family and should be treated that way. And we are driven by a shared passion to make sure every dog who isn't being loved, finds their way to a family. We care for each other and have created a community of people who love making a difference in this world.

Why Charlie Health?

Millions of people across the country are navigating mental health conditions, substance use disorders, and eating disorders, but too often, they’re met with barriers to care. From limited local options and long wait times to treatment that lacks personalization, behavioral healthcare can leave people feeling unseen and unsupported.

Charlie Health exists to change that. Our mission is to connect the world to life-saving behavioral health treatment. We deliver personalized, virtual care rooted in connection—between clients and clinicians, care teams, loved ones, and the communities that support them. By focusing on people with complex needs, we’re expanding access to meaningful care and driving better outcomes from the comfort of home.

As a rapidly growing organization, we're reaching more communities every day and building a team that’s redefining what behavioral health treatment can look like. If you're ready to use your skills to drive lasting change and help more people access the care they deserve, we’d love to meet you.

About the Role

Charlie Health is looking for a dynamic individual to serve as Clinical Admissions Therapist. The Clinical Admissions Therapist will be responsible for meeting with clients upon admission, building rapport, completing biopsychosocial assessments, and establishing treatment needs.

We’re a mission-driven team working to expand access to life-saving behavioral healthcare for people who need it most. Across all departments, we collaborate to deliver meaningful outcomes and build a more connected, effective model of care.   • Document client information in accordance with regulatory standards using electronic medical record
  • Assign treatment team members and group schedules while informing staff of new admissions
  • Interface with Admissions, Verification of Benefits, Utilization Review, and Clinical teams in facilitating intake
  • Collaborate with referral sources: hospitals, treatment centers, psychiatrists, therapists, and other behavioral health providers upon admission
  • Looking to cover the following shifts to meet the schedules and needs of our clients:

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Access to reliable technology resources to deliver uninterrupted, confidential, and compliant telehealth services
  • Ability to thrive in fast-paced environment while maintaining high attention to detail and quality of care

Requirements

  • Experience working with a wide range of ages, including children, teens, young adults, and adults preferred
  • Experience completing behavioral health assessments and admissions preferred

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.


What you will do

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role, the Executive Director will set the strategy and direction for Patient Support Operations within Patient Access & Reimbursement (PAR). The role will lead the contact center experience for patients and healthcare professionals (HCPs), advancing the people, processes, technology, automation, and AI capabilities that help customers get the support they need. Reporting to the Associate Vice President of PAR, the Executive Director will lead the teams and partners responsible for patient and HCP contact center activities across the portfolio. This leader will establish a high-performing, scalable operating model that delivers consistent, empathetic service while improving access, efficiency, quality, and customer experience. The Executive Director will work closely with PAR capability leaders, brand teams, Business Technology, Analytics, and external partners to turn customer needs and operational insights into clear priorities and measurable improvements.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Establish the vision, strategy, and operating model for Patient Support Operations, aligning contact center services with PAR’s enterprise priorities and the needs of patients, caregivers, and HCPs.
  • Lead patient and HCP contact center activities across the portfolio, ensuring a consistent, responsive, and customer-centered experience across channels.
  • Set the automation and AI strategy for contact center operations, identifying opportunities to simplify service, expand self-service, improve routing and agent support, and resolve customer needs more effectively.
  • Ensure AI and automation solutions are designed around customer needs, integrated with PAR capabilities and technology platforms, and supported by appropriate oversight, quality controls, and performance measures.
  • Lead operational planning and performance management, including service levels, access, quality, customer experience, productivity, capacity, and cost.
  • Establish clear performance goals and operating reviews; use customer feedback, contact drivers, call analytics, and operational data to identify issues and guide improvement.
  • Develop workforce and capacity strategies that align staffing, skills, training, and scheduling with customer demand and portfolio needs.
  • Build a strong quality, training, and continuous improvement model that equips teams to resolve customer needs accurately, consistently, and with empathy.
  • Partner with Patient Experience leaders, Field Capabilities, Patient Engagement & Affordability, Business Technology, Analytics, and brand teams to align contact center services with patient and HCP journeys.
  • Oversee contact center technology and process roadmaps with Business Technology and other partners, translating operational needs into scalable capabilities and ensuring effective implementation and adoption.
  • Lead vendor and partner relationships, establishing clear expectations, performance measures, governance, and accountability for service delivery and improvement.
  • Ensure operations follow applicable policies, privacy requirements, and compliance standards, with effective controls and escalation processes.
  • Represent Patient Support Operations in PAR leadership discussions and cross-functional forums; communicate performance, risks, investment needs, and recommendations clearly.

We are seeking a Senior Firmware Engineer with 5–8 years of professional embedded development experience who has strong experience building production embedded systems on modern wireless MCU platforms such as Espressif ESP32. In this role, you’ll work hands-on across the device firmware stack, from schematic review and board bring-up through production firmware, OTA, and certification.

What You’ll Be Working On

We dedicate each engineer to a single project in order to promote focus and minimize context switching. You will be developing production-grade firmware for connected devices from bring-up through production deployment and ongoing maintenance.

You will develop firmware across the full device lifecycle, including schematic review, board bring-up, driver integration, BLE provisioning, cloud connectivity, OTA updates, and certification readiness.

You will also participate in hardware debugging and validation using tools such as JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, and protocol sniffers to diagnose low-level issues across firmware, hardware, and network layers.

You’ll collaborate closely with hardware engineers, contract manufacturers, and cross-functional teams to deliver production-ready devices.

This role involves debugging complex, real-world interoperability issues across connected-device ecosystems, requiring deep protocol-level understanding and hands-on problem solving.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain production firmware for ESP32-based connected devices using ESP-IDF
  • Bring up new hardware and integrate drivers for sensors, actuators, LEDs, and other peripherals
  • Implement BLE provisioning, Wi-Fi connectivity, and secure cloud communication with AWS IoT Core over MQTT
  • Build and maintain reliable OTA update mechanisms, including rollback and staged rollouts
  • Debug and resolve issues across firmware, hardware, wireless, and cloud layers, from development through production
  • Partner with hardware engineers and contract manufacturers on factory flashing, device provisioning, and production readiness
  • Support certification (e.g., FCC) and hardware build phases (EVT/DVT/PVT)

  • Contribute to firmware CI/CD, test tooling, and technical documentation

Experience

  • 5–8 years professional embedded/firmware engineering in C/C++
  • Significant experience with Espressif ESP32 platforms using ESP-IDF, including RTOS-based development, OTA update mechanisms, low-level driver integration (I2C, SPI, UART, ADC, GPIO), and production firmware deployment.
  • Direct, demonstrable experience developing connected-device firmware on modern wireless platforms such as ESP32, including Bluetooth Low Energy, Wi-Fi, and related connectivity technologies.
  • Hands-on experience with wireless communication stacks such as BLE and Wi-Fi at the firmware level.
  • Experience debugging protocol-level communication issues, wireless connectivity problems, device provisioning flows, and interoperability challenges in connected-device ecosystems.
  • Experience connecting devices to cloud IoT platforms such as AWS IoT Core using MQTT over TLS, including certificate-based authentication and device state synchronization.
  • Experience integrating sensors, actuators, and peripherals such as RFID readers, accelerometers, motion sensors, LEDs, and pumps.
  • Comfortable reading technical specifications and translating them into production-quality firmware implementations.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Contributions to open-source ESP-IDF or nRF Connect SDK project
  • Background in adjacent protocols — Thread, Zigbee, Z-Wave, BLE Mesh — demonstrating breadth across the connected device landscape
  • History of working in a consultancy or product development firm where they've shipped across multiple product lines, not just one internal product
  • Comfort with hardware debug toolchains — JTAG/SWD, logic analyzers, protocol sniffers
  • Experience standing up CI/CD for firmware builds and automated test harnesses
  • Experience with Nordic nRF-series platforms using nRF Connect SDK
  • Familiarity with embedded security concepts such as secure boot, flash encryption, key management, device attestation, and secure firmware updates
  • Experience designing OTA update strategies with rollback and staged rollouts
  • Experience working with contract manufacturers on factory flashing, device provisioning, and production readiness
  • Experience supporting hardware through EVT/DVT/PVT builds and FCC certification
  • Familiarity with Protocol Buffers or similar serialization formats for device messaging
  • Python scripting for test tooling and device automation

Compensation & Benefits

Why Talkspace

Talkspace is a leading virtual behavioral healthcare provider committed to helping people lead healthier, happier lives through access to high-quality mental healthcare. At Talkspace, we believe that mental healthcare is core to overall health and should be available to everyone.

Talkspace pioneered the ability to text with a licensed therapist from anywhere and now offers a comprehensive suite of mental health services, including therapy for individuals, teens, and couples, as well as psychiatric treatment and medication management (18+). With Talkspace’s core therapy offerings, members are matched with one of thousands of licensed therapists within days and can engage in live video, audio, or chat sessions, and/or unlimited asynchronous text messaging sessions.

All care offered at Talkspace is delivered through an easy-to-use, fully-encrypted web and mobile platform that meets HIPAA, federal, and state regulatory requirements. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

Individuals seeking employment at Talkspace are considered without regard to race, color, religious creed, sex, national origin, citizenship status, age, physical or mental disability, sexual orientation, marital, parental, veteran or military status, unfavorable military discharge, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state or local law.

How do we define Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging at Talkspace?

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

jobs.description:
About the role

DRB builds the software that runs the modern car wash: point of sale, membership and recurring billing, payments, tunnel controls, and the analytics behind them. Our Solution Consulting team sits between customers, Sales, Product, and Customer Success, and exists to answer one question for every operator we work with: how do we help you grow, and what does the evidence say?

As a Solution Consultant you will do exactly that. You will dig into a customer's transaction, membership, and payment data to find what is actually happening in their business; frame the findings as clear recommendations an executive can act on; and build the demos, analyses, business cases, and prototypes that move enterprise deals and strategic accounts forward. You will use AI tools every day, not as a novelty but as the way we get quality work out faster than anyone expects.

This is a generalist seat on a small, flat team. You will not own a single lane. In a given month you may present a payment health review to a multi-site operator's leadership, build a pricing model for an RFP response, stand up a working AI prototype for a trade show, and write the talk track a sales rep uses to handle a competitive objection. If that range sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

What you'll do

Solution analysis and enterprise sales support
• Partner with Enterprise Sales on RFP responses, solution designs, hosting and pricing cost models, growth-incentive structures, and executive pitch narratives.
• Perform gap analyses to assess solution readiness for car wash operators moving to Patheon, DRB's latest platform — identifying functional, operational, and data gaps and defining what it takes to close them.
• Assess customer requirements against DRB's platform and be honest about fit, gaps, and workarounds; write the talk tracks that help reps navigate them.
• Build and maintain competitive intelligence and battlecards on the car wash technology landscape.
• Support Sales-to-Implementation handoffs and drive process improvements so what we sell is what gets delivered.

AI, prototyping, and innovation

  • Use AI tools (Claude and similar) as a daily working method to draft analyses, generate prototypes, structure research, and produce customer-ready deliverables at speed and quality.
    • Build working prototypes and demos: interactive HTML and Streamlit applications, AI-driven sales and service agents, kiosk and trade show experiences, and internal tools such as quoting integrations with Salesforce.
    • Contribute to DRB's internal AI enablement programs (prompt libraries, prototyping playbooks) that help colleagues across the business adopt the same methods.

Communication and enablement

  • Present to audiences from a single-site owner to a multi-site operator's executive team to Vontier leadership, adjusting depth and language for each without losing the substance.
    • Write clearly: executive summaries, customer-facing reports, Q&A documents, and internal briefs that people actually read and act on.
    • Represent DRB at trade shows and customer events, running demos and handling technical and commercial questions on the floor.
    Customer analytics and advisory
    • Lead data deep dives for enterprise and strategic accounts covering payments, membership, churn, and site performance, including benchmarking and post-migration health reviews.
    • Translate findings into prioritized recommendations, quantified business impact, and next steps, delivered in decks, written reports, and live discovery sessions with customer leadership.
    • Contribute to DRB's customer intelligence platform (Pulse) and the quarterly advisory cadence we run with top accounts, including new dashboards, report templates, and analytical methods.
    • Run joint discovery sessions with customers to surface the right questions, then coordinate internal owners across Product, Engineering, Legal, and Payments to get them answered.

Who you are

  • Four or more years in solution consulting, pre-sales engineering, customer analytics, management consulting, or a similar customer-facing analytical role, ideally in SaaS, payments, or retail/consumer subscription businesses.
    • Fluent with data: comfortable in SQL and a modern warehouse (we use Snowflake), able to build and defend an analysis end to end, and able to explain what the numbers mean to someone who will never look at the query.
    • A practitioner with AI tools. You already use them to do real work, you understand where they are reliable and where they are not, and you can show examples.
    • Structured thinker who can take an ambiguous customer or executive question, break it into what needs to be true, and get to a defensible answer with imperfect information.
    • Strong writer and presenter. You produce polished documents, decks, and prototypes without a designer, and you can hold a room.
    • Commercially minded: you understand how pricing, contracts, and incentives shape a deal, and you keep the customer's growth and DRB's margin in view at the same time.
    • Comfortable working across Sales, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Customer Success, driving things to closure without formal authority.

Nice to have

  • Experience in car wash, fuel and convenience, QSR, or another multi-site operator segment.
    • Familiarity with card payments and recurring billing.
    • Hands-on with Python, Streamlit, HTML/JavaScript, or Salesforce for building prototypes and internal tools.
    • Exposure to RFP and enterprise procurement processes, or to M&A and market evaluation work.

How we work

The Solution Consulting team is five people across data, technical, innovation, and marketing consulting disciplines, and everyone is expected to reach across those lines. We favor shipping a useful artifact this week over a perfect one next quarter, we use AI aggressively and hold the output to a professional standard, and we measure ourselves by whether customers grow and deals close. You will have direct exposure to DRB and Vontier leadership and a wide license to propose what we should build next.

The base compensation range for this position is $95,000.00 to $115,000.00 per annum. Your actual base salary will be determined based upon numerous factors which may include relevant experience, skills, location (labor market data), credentials (education, certifications), and internal equity.

About ComPsych

ComPsychⓇ is the worldwide leader in organizational mental health, well-being, and absence management, dedicated to igniting human potential in workplaces across the globe. Visit compsych.com to find out why 40% of the Fortune 500 choose ComPsych for their mental health and absence management needs.

About the Role

We're modernizing how ComPsych builds technology — new customer-facing web and mobile experiences, a unified design system, and AI-powered capabilities across our products. That means raising the engineering bar for how we design, build, and operate software, with Engineering, Product, and Design working together end to end.

We're looking for a Senior Software Engineer who has hands-on experience with modern, AI-led development practices and wants to help shape how our engineering organization builds software going forward. This is a high-leverage role: you'll spend more time on system design, task decomposition, and technical direction than on writing code line-by-line. You'll use AI tools to generate code, automated tests, and first-pass reviews, then apply your own judgment to validate and refine that output before it ships.

What You'll Do

AI changes what your time goes toward. You're still accountable for the full lifecycle — planning, design, code, tests, review, production — but your hands-on role in each shifts:

  • Plan and design as your core contribution. You own problem framing, sequencing, and tradeoffs with Product and Design, and the system design that follows — the data model, the API contracts, the failure modes.
  • Direct implementation rather than writing it line by line. Decompose the work, write the specs, and let AI agents build — dropping into the code yourself when debugging or complexity demands it.
  • Own testing as a design decision. You decide what needs coverage and at what level, direct AI to build it, and validate that the tests prove what they claim — not just that they pass.
  • Build security, reliability, and observability in from the start. They're design inputs, not production afterthoughts — the systems you ship can be operated safely and understood when they fail.
  • Review everything with the same rigor, regardless of author, and keep production judgment human. You're accountable for what ships whether you or an agent wrote it. Deployment calls, on-call response, and what an incident teaches you stay yours.
  • Raise the bar for how the team works with AI, coaching engineers to specify, delegate, and validate rather than hand-code everything themselves.

What We're Looking For

  • Deep server-side experience in a modern language such as Java, Python, C#, Kotlin, or Go. You've owned services end to end, not just features inside someone else's, and can pick up ours quickly.
  • Must have 5+ years of full stack development experience.
  • APIs and data models other people depend on: REST contracts, versioning, OAuth2/OIDC, schema design, and SQL that holds up under real load.
  • Async and event-driven systems in production — Kafka or comparable, idempotency, and a clear view of what at-least-once costs you downstream.
  • You've built and operated production systems at real scale on AWS or Azure — containers, Kubernetes or serverless, IaC, and CI/CD pipelines you've built, operated, or materially improved. You've carried the on-call load for them, so you know what “good” looks like independent of who or what wrote the code.
  • A testing strategy you can defend — what belongs at unit, integration, and contract level, and how you know a release is verifiable before it ships.
  • Reliability and security you've been accountable for: SLOs you’ve been paged against, incidents you led, OWASP and threat modeling applied — and PHI/HIPAA or comparable regulated-data experience.
  • Agentic AI is your primary development surface, and you catch what it gets subtly wrong. Not occasional autocomplete, not a hunch — you've shipped and operated real production systems working this way, and can point to what you caught before it shipped.

Bonus: LLM application engineering (RAG, retrieval quality, evals, LLM observability), or modern TypeScript frontend work against a design system.

USD $150,000.00 - USD $200,000.00 /Yr.

Diversity

Diversity encompasses the unique attributes of our employees as individuals. We value and embrace the richness arising from their varied backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences, which include, but are not limited to, age, ability, ethnicity, gender, race, and cultural background.

Equity

Equity refers to a fair and impartial workplace, aiming to ensure equal growth and advancement opportunities for all employees. This involves amplifying underrepresented voices, addressing unconscious biases, and providing inclusive, culturally competent mental health care.

Inclusion

Inclusion signifies the practice of granting equal access to opportunities and resources for all employees, particularly those who might otherwise be excluded or marginalized. It ensures that everyone feels a sense of belonging, value, support, and respect as an individual.

Belonging

Belonging reflects the affinity and positive relationships that develop among employees from diverse backgrounds when businesses actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion in the workplace.

Impact of a Sales Enablement Manager

As Sales Enablement Manager, you will own the onboarding path a seller follows in week one, the certification that shows they can execute, the kit that arrives before the deal does, and the measurement that shows it works. Our selling methodology only works if it holds when nobody is in the room. Our revenue enablement team makes that happen. One part of the team sets the methodology and coaches sellers directly. In close partnership with the Head of Sales Enablement, you will build and run the other part: the programs and systems that carry it every day.

Effective enablement goes beyond initial training to keep pace with a dynamic environment. As sellers join mid-quarter, product releases ship, and tools evolve, static frameworks in decks aren't enough. You will build robust systems and machinery that continuously support sellers and improve over time.

In this role you will report to the Senior Director, Customer Solutions.

What to expect

  • Programs and systems: Run onboarding and ramp for new sellers, with clear steps, checkpoints, and certification. Build the product change process as a system, so product updates reach sellers on time.

  • Sales plays and measurement: Build assets for sales plays and roll them out. Track ramp time, certification currency, and content usage. Report what the data shows and what to keep, change, or stop.

  • Content and knowledge: Build industry kits that sellers can use in a live deal. Deliver product trainings. Keep our knowledge base current and easy to search. Build a practice catalog for sellers, with AI roleplay where it helps.

  • AI as a practical tool: Use AI to speed up drafting, curation, and routine tasks. Test ideas quickly, keep what works, and protect quality while you move fast.

  • Cross-team partnership: Work with RevOps, Product Marketing, Product, and Engineering. Bring clear requirements and follow up after each launch, so sellers are ready when a release arrives.

  • Prioritization: You will have more requests than time. Prioritize the backlog, sequence the work, and explain your choices to your partners.

What you bring

  • Enablement program experience: Proven experience running sales enablement, revenue enablement, or GTM programs from start to finish in B2B technology, including programs that changed a measurable behavior.

  • Sales or solutions engineering background: Experience in sales or solutions engineering, with a clear sense of what sellers need in a live deal.

  • Builder mindset with AI: Experience turning repeated work into systems that run without you, and hands-on use of AI for drafting, summarizing, or automated workflows. Knowledge of where AI saves time and where it adds review work.

  • Clear thinking and measurement: Experience turning a goal into a defined problem, scope, steps, and success measure. Familiarity with choosing and tracking a leading indicator.

  • Technical product and tools: Familiarity with cloud infrastructure and developer workflows, enough to talk with technical buyers. Experience writing clear requirements for RevOps and working with enablement tools such as an LMS or knowledge base.

Bonus points

  • Experience setting up an LMS, knowledge management, conversation intelligence, or roleplay tool from scratch.

  • Experience building agents, skills, or automated workflows to support your own work or your team's work.

  • Experience enabling sellers for a platform, infrastructure, or developer tools product.

Where we hire

At Upsun, remote work isn't just a trend - it's our foundation. The freedom of remote work with the support of a diverse, global team has been our successful model for over a decade. Our culture celebrates flexibility and collaboration, and while we have team members in over 30 countries around the globe, we are currently focused on hiring for this role in France, Germany, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Although we’re unable to provide visa sponsorship at this time, we welcome applications from all qualified candidates who are legally authorized to work in these countries.

How we hire

We know that a great hire won’t meet every requirement that we’ve outlined. If you can see yourself elevating the team, we want to hear your story. Few of us would be here had we not taken a chance.

You can expect 4 interviews on Google Meet to follow the order below. Should you successfully move through the entire process you will have the opportunity to meet with a variety of Upsunners. Our goal is to ensure you can make the most informed decision on whether this role, and our culture aligns with what you’re looking for in your future working environment.

  2. 60 Minutes with Hiring Manager (Senior Director, Customer Solutions)

All roles require background checks.

You belong here
